images.text:
These days supermarkets keep flooding their shelves with different kinds of yogurts in different flavors.
Yogurt helps to balance the healthy bacteria in the body, and it is also a good source of calcium. Women's magazines claim that it even has qualities that happen to help the skin. When it is applied directly on the skin, it is supposed to heal burns. You should aim to eat it every day. But yogurt is not a new fad. It has been around for thousands of years.

Yogurt is a staple in many cultures known for people who live long lives. Legend has it that Methuselah, who was famous in the Bible for living over 900 years, ate yogurt.
It is also said that King Solomon, the biblical character known for his wisdom, also enjoyed it.
Yogurt is not only made from cow's milk. Supposedly, goat's milk yogurt was eaten by the biblical patriarch Abraham. It is also believed that Genghis Khan, the great Mongol warrior, ate a lot of yak milk yogurt.

Yogurt is easy to make at home. This is how:
Yogurt is fermented from milk and from live cultures. To make it, a spoonful of existing yogurt is supposed to be put into a cup of milk.
The culture in the existing yogurt is supposed to react with the milk and in a few days yogurt is made. Flavors are then supposed to be added to improve the taste. I don't know about you, but I can't stand eating plain yogurt!

Gerunds and Infinitives

A gerund is a verb ending with -ing. Examples: doing, watching , talking , playing.
An infinitive is when a verb is preceded by the word to. Examples: to do,to watch,to talk, to play.

Verbs commonly followed by a gerund:
Verbs that express likes/dislikes:
  • like
  • love
  • enjoy
  • dislike
  • hate

Example:
Tom disliked eating plain yogurt.
like/love/hate can also be followed by an infinitive.
Some other verbs that are followed by a gerund:

• anticipate
  • can't stand
  • delay
  • complete
  • involve
  • keep
  • risk
These are some verbs that are followed by an infinitive:

• hope
  • proceed
  • seem
  • decide
  • help
  • happen

Example:
You should aim to eat yogurt every day.
You use Infinitives after adjectives.

Example:
Yogurt is easy to make at home.
These days supermarkets keep flooding their shelves with different kinds of yogurts in different flavors.
Yogurt helps to balance the healthy bacteria in the body, and it is also a good source of calcium.
Women's magazines claim that it even has qualities that happen to help the skin.
I don't know about you, but I can't stand eating plain yogurt!
Be Supposed To
You use the structure be supposed to when you want to talk about expectations, obligations or arrangements.
You can use be supposed to to talk about situations in the past, present or future.

The structure is:

Subject + To be + supposed to + verb
When it is applied directly on the skin, yogurt is supposed to heal burns.

**Pronunciation tip**:
When you say be supposed to, you link the /d/ and /t/ sounds together.

Like this: Be suppose_to
To make it, a spoonful of existing yogurt is supposed to be put into a cup of milk.
The culture in the existing yogurt is supposed to react with the milk and in a few days yogurt is made.
Flavors are then supposed to be added to improve the taste.
